questions.question: When acid reacts with a metal carbonate, it forms:

options.text: a base and water as products

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**salt, carbon dioxide, and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **acid** reacts with a **metal carbonate**, the chemical reaction consistently produces three distinct products: a **salt**, **carbon dioxide** gas, and **water**.
 
• The general chemical word equation for this interaction is: **Acid + Metal Carbonate → Salt + Water + Carbon Dioxide**.
 
• The formation of **carbon dioxide** is a characteristic feature of this reaction, usually manifesting as rapid **effervescence** or bubbling when the acid makes contact with the carbonate.
 
• The specific **salt** produced depends on the **metal** present in the carbonate and the **anion** of the acid used; for instance, **Hydrochloric Acid** reacting with **Calcium Carbonate** produces **Calcium Chloride**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• A **base** and **water** are typically products of a reaction between an acid and a metal oxide or hydroxide (neutralization), not a carbonate. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Hydrogen gas** is released when an **acid** reacts with a **metal**, but not when it reacts with a metal carbonate. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While a gas is produced, the other products (salt and water) are usually in aqueous or liquid states, not necessarily a **solid precipitate** in all cases. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Identification of CO2**: The **carbon dioxide** gas produced in this reaction can be identified using the **lime water test**. When the gas is passed through **lime water** (calcium hydroxide), it turns **milky** due to the formation of insoluble **calcium carbonate**.
 
• **Metal Hydrogen Carbonates**: Also known as **bicarbonates**, these compounds react with **acids** in the exact same manner as carbonates, yielding a **salt**, **water**, and **carbon dioxide**. An example is the reaction of **Sodium Bicarbonate (Baking Soda)** with **citric acid** or **vinegar**.
 
• **Salt Formation**: If **Sulfuric Acid** is used, the resulting salt will be a **sulfate**. If **Nitric Acid** is used, the salt will be a **nitrate**. The **metal** component comes directly from the **metal carbonate** reactant.
 
• **Nature of Carbonates**: Metal carbonates are considered **basic** in nature. Therefore, their reaction with **acids** is technically a form of **neutralization**, though the presence of the **carbonate group (CO3)** leads to the additional byproduct of **carbon dioxide**.
 
• **Real-world Examples**: This chemical principle is used in **fire extinguishers** (where acid and carbonate react to release CO2 to smother flames) and is also the reason why **acid rain** causes the **erosion** of statues and buildings made of **limestone** or **marble**, which are forms of **calcium carbonate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Equation for Calcium Carbonate**: A standard laboratory example is **2HCl + CaCO3 → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2**. This reaction involves **Hydrochloric Acid** and **Calcium Carbonate** (found in **eggshells** and **chalk**).
 
• **Effervescence**: The term **effervescence** refers to the escape of **gas** from an **aqueous solution** and the **foaming** or **fizzing** that results from that release.
 
• **Limestone Weathering**: In **nature**, when **rainwater** (which is slightly acidic due to dissolved CO2) reacts over long periods with **limestone** rocks, it leads to the formation of **caves** and **sinkholes** through this specific chemical breakdown.

questions.question: Why is conservation of petroleum important?

options.text: Petroleum does not affect the environment adversely.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Petroleum is a non-renewable resource.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Petroleum**, also known as **crude oil**, is a naturally occurring liquid found beneath the Earth's surface. It is classified as a **fossil fuel** because it is formed from the remains of ancient marine organisms.
 
• Conservation is critical because petroleum is a **non-renewable resource**. This means that once it is consumed, it cannot be replaced or replenished within a human timeframe, as its formation process takes **millions of years**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Unlike **renewable resources** like solar or wind energy, which are inexhaustible, the global supply of petroleum is **finite**. The rate at which humanity extracts and uses it far exceeds the geological rate of its creation. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While petroleum reserves are found in various parts of the world, they are not **abundant** in an infinite sense; they are depletable assets that are being rapidly exhausted. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The extraction, refining, and combustion of petroleum have significant **negative impacts** on the environment, including **air pollution**, **oil spills**, and the release of **greenhouse gases**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation Process**: Petroleum is formed through the decomposition of organic matter (mostly **zooplankton** and **algae**) buried under layers of **sedimentary rock**. Over **millions of years**, high **pressure** and **heat** transform this matter into liquid hydrocarbons.
 
• **Economic Value**: Often referred to as **"Black Gold,"** petroleum is the backbone of the modern global economy. It is the primary source of energy for **transportation** and acts as a vital raw material for the **petrochemical industry**.
 
• **Environmental Consequences**: Burning petroleum-based fuels like **gasoline** and **diesel** releases **carbon dioxide (CO2)**, a major contributor to **global warming** and **climate change**. It also produces pollutants like **sulfur dioxide** and **nitrogen oxides**.
 
• **Global Distribution**: The largest proven reserves of petroleum are concentrated in regions such as the **Middle East** (e.g., **Saudi Arabia**, **Iran**, **Iraq**), **Venezuela**, **Russia**, and the **United States**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Refining**: Crude oil is processed in **refineries** through a method called **fractional distillation**. This process separates the oil into various products like **petrol**, **kerosene**, **lubricating oil**, **paraffin wax**, and **asphalt**.
 
• **Conservation Methods**: Reducing petroleum dependency involves shifting to **electric vehicles (EVs)**, improving **public transportation**, and increasing the use of **biofuels** or **renewable energy** sources.
 
• **Sustainable Development**: Conserving fossil fuels aligns with the principles of **sustainable development**, which aims to meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of **future generations** to meet their own needs.
 
• **By-products**: Beyond fuel, petroleum is used to manufacture **plastics**, **synthetic rubbers**, **chemical fertilizers**, **pesticides**, and even some **pharmaceuticals**.

questions.question: Which of the following birth control methods can cause hormonal imbalance, and probably health issues?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oral contraceptive pills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Oral contraceptive pills** are a popular method of **birth control** used by **females**, which involves the **oral administration** of small doses of either **progestogens** or **progestogen-estrogen combinations**.
 
• These pills function by **inhibiting ovulation** and **implantation**, and they also alter the quality of **cervical mucus** to prevent or retard the entry of **sperms** into the **uterus**.
 
• Because they introduce **exogenous hormones** into the female body to override the natural **menstrual cycle**, they can lead to a significant **hormonal imbalance**.
 
• Common **health issues** or side effects associated with these pills include **nausea**, **abdominal pain**, **breakthrough bleeding**, **irregular menstrual cycles**, **breast tenderness**, and **weight gain**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Oral contraceptive pills.***
 
• Other methods like **condoms** or **Copper-T** do not primarily function by altering the systemic **hormonal levels** of the user, making **oral pills** the most likely cause of such imbalances.

questions.question: For a distinct echo to be heard, the minimum time interval between the original sound and the reflected sound should be approximately ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1 s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **echo** is the phenomenon where a sound is heard again after it is **reflected** back from a hard surface like a wall, mountain, or cliff.
 
• To hear a distinct echo, the sensation of the original sound must have faded from the human brain. The **persistence of hearing** for a human ear is approximately **0.1 seconds**.
 
• This means that the **time interval** between the original sound and the reflected sound must be at least **0.1 s** for the human brain to distinguish them as two separate sounds.
 
• If the reflected sound arrives in less than **0.1 s**, the two sounds merge, and we hear a prolonged sound rather than a distinct echo.
 
• The total distance covered by the sound (from the source to the obstacle and back) must be such that the time taken is **0.1 s** or more. At a standard speed of sound in air (approx. **344 m/s** at **22°C**), this total distance is **34.4 meters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calculation of Minimum Distance:**
 
 
• The minimum distance required to hear an echo can be calculated using the formula: **Distance = (Speed × Time) / 2**.
 
• Using the standard speed of **344 m/s** and the minimum time of **0.1 s**, the distance is (**344 × 0.1) / 2 = 17.2 meters**.
 
• Therefore, to hear a clear echo, the obstacle must be at least **17.2 meters** away from the source of the sound.
 
 
 
• **Reverberation:**
 
 
• When sound is reflected multiple times in a closed space (like a large hall), the reflections persist and blur the original sound; this is known as **reverberation**.
 
• Unlike an echo, which is a single distinct reflection, **reverberation** is the persistence of sound due to repeated reflections arriving in less than **0.1 s**.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Speed of Sound:**
 
 
• The speed of sound varies with the **temperature** of the medium. For every **1 degree Celsius** rise in temperature, the speed of sound increases by approximately **0.6 m/s**.
 
• As the speed of sound increases with temperature, the **minimum distance** required to hear an echo also increases on a hot day.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nature of Surfaces:** Echoes are best heard when the reflecting surface is **large, hard, and distant**. Soft surfaces like curtains or carpets absorb sound and prevent echoes.
 
• **Applications of Reflection:** The principle of sound reflection and echo is used in **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) to measure the depth of the sea and in **Ultrasound** imaging for medical diagnostics.
 
• **Speed in Media:** Sound travels fastest in **solids**, followed by **liquids**, and slowest in **gases**. In water, the speed of sound is roughly **1500 m/s**, which would significantly increase the minimum distance needed for an echo compared to air.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about olfactory indicators is correct?

options.text: Onion and vanilla both lose their smell in acidic conditions.
In basic solutions, vanilla essence retains its original sweet smell.
In basic solutions, the smell of onion extract remains unchanged.
In acidic solutions, onion extract retains its characteristic smell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In acidic solutions, onion extract retains its characteristic smell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are substances whose **odour** or **smell** changes depending on whether they are mixed with an **acidic** or a **basic** solution.
 
• **Onion extract** is a common olfactory indicator. When it is treated with an **acid** (like dilute **Hydrochloric acid**), its characteristic pungent smell does not go away and remains **detectable**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• In contrast, when **onion extract** is treated with a **base** (like **Sodium Hydroxide**), its characteristic smell **disappears** or cannot be detected. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Vanilla essence** also acts as an olfactory indicator; it retains its **sweet smell** in **acidic** conditions but **loses** it completely in **basic** solutions. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Both **onion** and **vanilla** do **not** lose their smell in **acidic** conditions; they only lose their smell when exposed to **alkaline** or **basic** substances. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is In acidic solutions, onion extract retains its characteristic smell.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Indicators:**
 
 
• **Natural Indicators:** These are obtained from natural sources like **plants**. Examples include **Litmus** (extracted from **Lichens**), **Turmeric**, and **Red Cabbage** extract. **Turmeric** stays **yellow** in **acid** but turns **reddish-brown** in **base**.
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:** These are **man-made** chemical substances. **Phenolphthalein** remains **colorless** in **acidic** solutions but turns **pink** in **basic** solutions. **Methyl orange** turns **red** in **acid** and **yellow** in **base**.
 
• **Olfactory Indicators:** These are particularly useful in **chemistry laboratories** for **visually impaired** students, as they can identify the nature of a substance by **smell** rather than **color change**.
 
 
 
• **Clove Oil:** It is another prominent **olfactory indicator**. Like onion and vanilla, the **smell of clove oil** can be detected in the presence of an **acid**, but it **vanishes** when mixed with a **base**.
 
• **Practical Application:** To test if a substance is a base using an olfactory indicator, one can rub **onion juice** on a strip of cloth and then add the test solution. If the smell of the onion **disappears**, the solution is **basic** in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acids:** These are substances that produce **Hydrogen ions (H+)** in **aqueous solutions**. They have a **sour taste** and turn **blue litmus red**.
 
• **Bases:** These are substances that produce **Hydroxide ions (OH-)** in **aqueous solutions**. They have a **bitter taste**, a **soapy feel**, and turn **red litmus blue**.
 
• **Neutralization:** When an **acid** and a **base** react, they produce **salt and water**. This reaction often eliminates the **indicator** changes associated with the individual **pH** levels.
 
• The **pH scale** ranges from **0 to 14**, where **7** is **neutral**, values **less than 7** are **acidic**, and values **greater than 7** are **basic**.
</ul

What is the primary function of the structure 'A' attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum in the given diagram?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manufacturing proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Structure **'A'** in the diagram represents **ribosomes**, which are the fundamental cellular organelles responsible for **protein synthesis**.
 
• Ribosomes are often found attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**, giving it a distinctive "rough" or granular appearance under an electron microscope.
 
• The primary role of these attached **ribosomes** is to translate **messenger RNA (mRNA)** into **polypeptide chains**, which then enter the **lumen** of the **RER** for proper folding and processing. ***Hence, the option regarding manufacturing proteins is correct.***
 
• These proteins produced on the **RER** are typically destined for **secretion** out of the cell, incorporation into the **plasma membrane**, or for use within **lysosomes**.
 
• Ribosomes function by linking **amino acids** together in a specific order dictated by the **genetic code**, a process known as **translation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**:
 
 
• The **ER** is a continuous membrane system that forms a series of flattened sacs within the **cytoplasm** of **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• It is divided into two types: **Rough ER** (studded with **ribosomes**) and **Smooth ER** (lacking **ribosomes**).
 
• The **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** is primarily involved in the **production of fat molecules** (lipids), **steroids**, and the **detoxification** of metabolic byproducts.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus**:
 
 
• The **nucleus** is the "control center" of the cell and is responsible for **storing genetic material** in the form of **DNA** (Deoxyribonucleic acid).
 
• It coordinates cell activities like **growth**, **intermediary metabolism**, and **reproduction** (cell division).
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**:
 
 
• These are membrane-bound organelles containing **digestive enzymes** (hydrolases) responsible for the **digestion of food particles**, damaged organelles, and foreign substances like **bacteria**.
 
• They are often referred to as the **"suicide bags"** of the cell because they can digest the cell itself if it becomes damaged or dies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery**: **Ribosomes** were first identified in the **mid-1950s** by **George Emil Palade**, who used electron microscopy to observe them as dense particles or granules.
 
• **Structure**: A ribosome is composed of two subunits—the **large subunit** and the **small subunit**—which come together during the process of **protein manufacturing**.
 
• **Composition**: They are chemically composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and dozens of distinct **proteins**.
 
• **Location**: While many are attached to the **Rough ER**, "free" **ribosomes** also exist in the **cytosol**, where they synthesize proteins that function within the **cytoplasm** itself.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions will increase the rate of evaporation of a liquid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in wind speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is a surface phenomenon where liquid changes into vapor at any temperature below its **boiling point**.
 
• **Increase in wind speed**: With an **increase in wind speed**, the particles of water vapor move away with the wind. This decreases the amount of water vapor in the surrounding atmosphere, thereby increasing the rate of evaporation. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Humidity**: Humidity is the amount of water vapor present in the air. The air around us cannot hold more than a definite amount of water vapor at a given **temperature**. If the amount of water in the air is already high (high humidity), the rate of evaporation decreases. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Temperature**: With an **increase in temperature**, more particles get enough **kinetic energy** to go into the vapor state. Therefore, a **decrease in temperature** leads to a slower rate of evaporation. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Surface Area**: Since evaporation is a **surface phenomenon**, if the **surface area is increased**, the rate of evaporation increases. For example, while putting clothes for drying up, we spread them out. A **decrease in surface area** will reduce the rate. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Evaporation:**
 
 
• In a liquid, a small fraction of particles at the surface, having higher **kinetic energy**, is able to break away from the forces of attraction of other particles and gets converted into vapor.
 
• Unlike **boiling**, which is a **bulk phenomenon** occurring at a specific **boiling point** (e.g., **100 degrees Celsius** for water at **1 atmospheric pressure**), evaporation occurs at all temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation Causes Cooling:**
 
 
• The particles of liquid absorb energy from the surrounding to regain the energy lost during evaporation. This absorption of energy from the surroundings makes the surroundings cold.
 
• **Example 1**: During **summer**, people sprinkle water on the roof or open ground because the large **latent heat of vaporization** of water helps to cool the hot surface.
 
• **Example 2**: We wear **cotton clothes** in summer because cotton, being a good absorber of water, helps in absorbing **sweat** and exposing it to the atmosphere for easy evaporation, which cools our body.
 
 
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization:**

• **Pressure:** The rate of evaporation is **inversely proportional** to the **atmospheric pressure**. When the pressure is low, it is easier for molecules to escape into the air.
 
• **Practical Application**: **Desert coolers** work better on a **hot dry day** because the high temperature and low humidity increase the rate of evaporation of water, resulting in better cooling.
</ul

questions.question: The commercial unit of electric energy is kilowatt hour (kW h). Which of the following is the correct value of 1kWh?

The correct answer is __**3.6 x 10⁶ Joule**__.

__
 
• The **kilowatt-hour (kWh)** is the **commercial unit** of **electrical energy**. It is commonly used by electricity providers to bill consumers for the total amount of energy consumed over a period.
 
• To find the value of **1 kWh** in **Joules**, we use the relationship **Energy = Power x Time**. Here, the **power** is **1 kilowatt** and the **time** is **1 hour**.
 
• **1 kilowatt (kW)** is equal to **1000 Watts**. Since **1 Watt** is defined as **1 Joule per second (J/s)**, **1000 Watts** is equivalent to **1000 Joules per second**.
 
• **1 hour** consists of **60 minutes**, and each minute has **60 seconds**. Therefore, **1 hour** equals **3600 seconds** (60 x 60).
 
• The calculation for conversion is: **1 kWh = 1000 J/s x 3600 s**, which results in **3,600,000 Joules**. In scientific notation, this is expressed as **3.6 x 10⁶ Joules**. ***Hence, the value of 1 kWh is 3.6 x 10⁶ Joules.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrical Energy:** This refers to the energy derived from electric potential energy or kinetic energy. The **SI unit** of energy is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule** in the **19th century**.
 
• **Power:** It is defined as the **rate** at which work is done or energy is transferred. The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, named after **James Watt**. **1 Watt** is equal to **1 Joule per second**.
 
• **Need for Commercial Units:** Because the **Joule** is a very small unit of energy, it is inconvenient for expressing large quantities of energy used in **homes, industries, and commercial establishments**. For these purposes, the larger unit **kilowatt-hour** is used.
 
• **Measuring Consumption:** Household electricity meters measure energy in **"units"**. In this context, **1 unit** of electricity is exactly equal to **1 kilowatt-hour**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **1 Joule:** It is the work done when a force of **one Newton** displaces an object by **one meter** in the direction of the force. It is also the energy dissipated as heat when an electric current of **one Ampere** passes through a resistance of **one Ohm** for **one second**.
 
• **History of the Unit:** The term **Board of Trade (B.O.T.) unit** was formerly used in the **United Kingdom** as a synonym for **kilowatt-hour**. This was the standard for electrical billing starting in the **year 1882**.
 
• **Conversions:** While **1 kWh** is **3.6 x 10⁶ Joules**, other related units include the **calorie** (approx **4.184 Joules**) and the **British Thermal Unit (BTU)** (approx **1055 Joules**).
 
• **Efficiency:** Understanding **kWh** helps in calculating the **efficiency** of electrical appliances by determining how many **Joules** of energy they consume to perform a specific amount of work.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the mass of an object?

options.text: It stays the same no matter where the object is.
It changes from place to place.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It stays the same no matter where the object is**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is a fundamental property of matter that represents the total amount of **matter** or **atoms** contained within an object.
 
• Statement 1: It depends on gravity. This statement is **incorrect**. **Mass** is independent of **gravitational pull**. It is **weight** that depends on the **acceleration due to gravity** (**g**).
 
• Statement 2: It stays the same no matter where the object is. This statement is **correct** because **mass** is an **intrinsic property**. Whether the object is on **Earth**, the **Moon**, or in **outer space**, the quantity of matter it contains does not change. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement 3: It increases at pole. This statement is **incorrect**. While the **weight** of an object increases at the **Earth's poles** because the **Earth** is not a perfect sphere and the **gravitational force** is stronger there, the **mass** remains **constant**.
 
• Statement 4: It changes from place to place. This statement is **incorrect**. This is a characteristic of **weight**, which varies depending on the **altitude**, **latitude**, or the **celestial body** the object is placed upon.
 
• **Mass** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it only has **magnitude** and no **direction**. It can never be **zero** for a physical object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Measurement Units**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of **mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• Other common units include **grams (g)**, **milligrams (mg)**, and **tonnes (1,000 kg)**.
 
 
 
• **Relationship with Weight**:
 
 
• **Weight** is the force exerted by **gravity** on an object. It is calculated using the formula **W = m × g**, where **m** is **mass** and **g** is **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²** on **Earth**).
 
• Since **g** varies at different locations, **weight** changes, but **mass** (**m**) remains the same.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**:
 
 
• **Mass** is often described as a measure of **inertia**. **Inertia** is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its **state of motion**.
 
• An object with a larger **mass** has greater **inertia**, making it harder to start moving, stop, or change its **direction**.
 
 
 
• **Measuring Instruments**:
 
 
• **Mass** is typically measured using a **beam balance** or a **physical balance**, which compares an unknown mass against **standard masses**.
 
• **Weight** is measured using a **spring balance**, which measures the **force** of gravity pulling on the object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation of Mass**: In **classical physics** and **chemical reactions**, the **Law of Conservation of Mass** states that **mass** can neither be created nor destroyed; it only changes forms.
 
• **Difference on the Moon**: The **gravity** on the **Moon** is only **1/6th** of that on **Earth**. If an object has a **mass** of **60 kg**, it will still have a **mass** of **60 kg** on the **Moon**, but its **weight** will drop from **588 N** (on Earth) to approximately **98 N**.
 
• **Atomic Mass**: On a microscopic scale, the **mass** of an atom is measured in **Atomic Mass Units (amu)**, defined as **1/12th** of the **mass** of a **carbon-12 atom**.
 
• **Relativistic Mass**: According to **Einstein's Theory of Relativity**, as an object approaches the **speed of light**, its **relativistic mass** increases, though its **rest mass** remains unchanged.
</ul

__
 
• The phenomenon of **dispersion of light** was first explained by the English physicist and mathematician **Sir Isaac Newton** in the year **1666**.
 
• Through his landmark experiments with **glass prisms**, Newton demonstrated that **white light** is not a single entity but is actually composed of a **spectrum** of different colors.
 
• He observed that when a narrow beam of sunlight passes through a triangular glass prism, it splits into a band of seven colors, commonly known as **VIBGYOR** (**Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red**).
 
• Newton concluded that different colors of light bend through different angles with respect to the incident beam as they pass through the prism. **Violet light** undergoes the **maximum deviation**, while **red light** undergoes the **minimum deviation**.
 
• To confirm that the prism was not adding color to the light, he placed a second identical prism in an inverted position with respect to the first one, which allowed the separated colors to **recombine** into **white light**.

• **Dispersion**: This is defined as the splitting of a composite beam of light into its constituent colors when it passes through a transparent medium like a **prism** or a **water droplet**.
 
• **Refractive Index and Wavelength**: The cause of dispersion is that the **Refractive Index** of a material varies for different **wavelengths**. Since each color has a specific wavelength, they travel at different speeds within the medium, leading to different degrees of refraction.
 
• **Christiaan Huygens**: A Dutch scientist who proposed the **Wave Theory of Light** in **1678**. He suggested that light travels in the form of longitudinal waves through a hypothetical medium called "ether."
 
• **James Clerk Maxwell**: A Scottish scientist who developed the theory of **Electromagnetism** in the **1860s**. He mathematically proved that light is an **electromagnetic wave** that can travel through a vacuum.
 
• **Albert Einstein**: A German-born physicist who explained the **Photoelectric Effect** in **1905**, for which he received the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1921**. He introduced the concept of **photons**, establishing the particle nature of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Natural Dispersion**: A **rainbow** is a prime example of dispersion of sunlight caused by **water droplets** in the atmosphere. This process involves **refraction**, **dispersion**, and **Total Internal Reflection (TIR)**.
 
• **Visible Spectrum**: The range of wavelengths visible to the human eye is approximately **400 nm to 700 nm**. **Violet** has the **shortest wavelength** and highest frequency, while **red** has the **longest wavelength** and lowest frequency.
 
• **Newton's Opticks**: Isaac Newton published his detailed findings on light and color in his famous book titled **"Opticks"** in **1704**, which laid the foundation for modern physical optics.
</ul

The correct answer is __**Tall Plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor Johann Mendel**, known as the **Father of Genetics**, conducted his historic experiments on the **Garden Pea** (**Pisum sativum**) for **seven years** between **1856** and **1863**.
 
• He selected **seven pairs** of contrasting traits to study the **inheritance patterns** in living organisms.
 
• **Stem Height**: Mendel observed that **Tall** height is the **dominant trait**, while **Dwarf** height is the **recessive trait**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct and statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Seed Shape**: The **dominant trait** is **Round**, whereas the **Wrinkled** shape is **recessive**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Seed Color**: In pea plants, **Yellow** seeds are **dominant** and **Green** seeds are **recessive**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pod Color**: Interestingly, for pods, **Green** is the **dominant trait** and **Yellow** is the **recessive trait**, which is the opposite of the seed color dominance.
 
• **Flower Color and Position**: The **Violet** flower color is **dominant** over **White**, and the **Axial** position of flowers is **dominant** over the **Terminal** position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reasons for choosing Pea Plants**:
 
 
• The **Pisum sativum** plant is **bisexual** and naturally undergoes **self-pollination**, making it easy to produce **pure-breeding** lines.
 
• It has a **short life cycle**, allowing for the study of multiple generations in a short time, and produces a **large number of offspring** (seeds).
 
• The plant exhibits **distinct and easily detectable contrasting traits**, which were crucial for **Mendel’s** statistical analysis.
 
 
 
• **Mendel’s Laws of Inheritance**:
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**: In a **heterozygous** individual (Tt), the **dominant allele** (T) expresses itself, masking the effect of the **recessive allele** (t).
 
• **Law of Segregation**: During **gamete formation**, the two alleles for a trait **segregate** so that each gamete receives only one allele.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment**: Different traits are inherited **independently** of each other, provided the genes are on different chromosomes.
 
 
 
• **Ratios in Genetics**:
 
 
• In a **Monohybrid cross** (studying one trait like height), the **phenotypic ratio** in the **F2 generation** is **3:1** (3 Tall : 1 Dwarf), and the **genotypic ratio** is **1:2:1** (1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).
 
• In a **Dihybrid cross** (studying two traits), the **phenotypic ratio** is **9:3:3:1**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dominant vs. Recessive**: A **dominant trait** is one that appears in the **F1 generation** after crossing two **pure-breeding** parents of contrasting traits. A **recessive trait** is one that remains **latent** in the **F1 generation** but reappears in the **F2 generation**.
 
• **Alleles**: These are alternative forms of a **gene** (e.g., T and t). If both alleles are the same, the organism is **homozygous** (TT or tt); if they are different, it is **heterozygous** (Tt).
 
• **Phenotype and Genotype**: **Phenotype** refers to the **observable physical characteristics** (e.g., Tall), while **Genotype** refers to the **genetic makeup** (e.g., Tt).
</ul

questions.question: Mahi would need twice as much time as Neha and Asha combined, while Asha would require three times as much time as Neha and Mahi combined to complete a certain task. If all three friends work together, they can finish the task in 20 days. How many days would Neha take to complete the same task on her own?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let efficiencies be M, N, A

M takes double time of (N + A) ⇒ M = (N + A)/2

A takes triple time of (N + M) ⇒ A = (N + M)/3

Substitute ⇒ A = (3N)/5 and M = (4N)/5

Total work rate = N + M + A = (12N)/5 = 1/20 ⇒ N = 1/48

**∴ Answer = 48 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mahi takes twice the time of (Neha + Asha)

Asha takes three times the time of (Neha + Mahi)

All together complete work in 20 days

**Formula used:**

Efficiency ∝ 1 / Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let efficiencies be M, N, A

⇒ Mahi takes twice time ⇒ M = (N + A)/2

⇒ Asha takes three times time ⇒ A = (N + M)/3

⇒ Substitute M in second equation:

⇒ A = (N + (N + A)/2)/3

⇒ 3A = (2N + N + A)/2

⇒ 6A = 3N + A

⇒ 5A = 3N ⇒ A = 3N/5

⇒ M = (N + A)/2 = (N + 3N/5)/2 = 4N/5

⇒ Total efficiency = N + M + A = N + 4N/5 + 3N/5 = 12N/5

⇒ Given total time = 20 ⇒ efficiency = 1/20

⇒ 12N/5 = 1/20

⇒ N = 1/48

⇒ Time taken by Neha = 48 days

**∴ The correct answer is 48 days.**

questions.question: One pipe can fill a tank in 8 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 40 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 8 and 40 = 40 units.

Efficiency of filling pipe = 40 ÷ 8 = +5 units/min.

Efficiency of emptying pipe = 40 ÷ 40 = −1 unit/min.

Net efficiency when both are open = 5 − 1 = 4 units/min.

Time to fill half the tank (20 units) = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by filling pipe = 8 minutes

Time taken by emptying pipe = 40 minutes

**Calculation:**

Let the total work (capacity) be the LCM of 8 and 40.

⇒ Net efficiency of both pipes when opened together = 5 − 1 = 4 units/minute.

⇒ Total work to fill half the tank = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 units.

⇒ Time taken to fill half the tank = Target Work ÷ Net Efficiency = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank, so its rate of work is taken as positive. An outlet pipe empties the tank, so its rate of work is taken as negative.

Combined Rate Formula

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 29, 90, 50, 26, 36, 77, 86, 33 and 41 is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the Assumed Mean Method (Deviation Method). Let the Assumed Mean = 50.

Deviations from 50 = −21, +40, 0, −24, −14, +27, +36, −17, −9.

Sum of deviations = (+40 + 27 + 36) − (21 + 24 + 14 + 17 + 9) = 103 − 85 = +18.

Average deviation = +18 ÷ 9 = +2.

Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + Average deviation = 50 + 2 = 52.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the simplest and most widely used measure of an average. It involves finding the sum of a given group of values and then dividing that sum by the total count of numbers.

Assumed Mean Method

This method is highly useful in reducing calculations for large data groups. Formula: Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + (Sum of Deviations ÷ Number of Observations).

Weighted Average

Used when certain data points hold more weight or frequency. Formula: Weighted Mean = Σ(wᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ.

Empirical Relationship

For moderately skewed distributions, the mean, median, and mode are fundamentally related by the formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.question: A cricketer has an average of 97 runs over 6 innings. If he scores 231 runs in the 7th inning, by how many runs (rounded off to the nearest whole number) does his average score increase?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial total = 97 × 6 = 582

New total = 582 + 231 = 813

New average = 813 ÷ 7 ≈ 116.14

Increase = 116.14 − 97 ≈ 19.14 ≈ 19

**∴ Answer = 19 runs**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 6 innings = 97

Runs in 7th inning = 231

**Formula used:**

Average = Total runs ÷ Number of innings

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total runs in 6 innings = 97 × 6 = 582

⇒ Total runs in 7 innings = 582 + 231 = 813

⇒ New average = 813 ÷ 7 = 116.14

• The **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA)** is a global initiative launched to focus on the protection and conservation of **seven** major big cat species: **Tiger**, **Lion**, **Leopard**, **Snow Leopard**, **Cheetah**, **Jaguar**, and **Puma**.
